slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Single record, no backup/mirror/generation counter. Valid iff logical byte 0x000=='W' (0x57), logical byte 0x171 (369)=='W' (0x57), and sum8 over logical 0x000..0x170 (369 bytes) equals stored byte at logical 0x172 (370). Loader sets RAM save-present boolean (struct+0x83) from the two magics and valid flag (struct+0x88) from the checksum; consumers' use of these flags is not in the corpus. Offsets are logical (RAM buffer) offsets: .sav file offset = (L & ~7) | (7 - (L & 7)) due to per-8-byte-block byte reversal in FUN_08049504. Bytes 0x173..0x1FF of the 512-byte image are a written-but-unused zero tail.

checksums.name: save_record_sum8
checksums.formula_detail: stored == (sum of logical bytes 0x000..0x170 inclusive, 369 bytes, including magic byte at 0x000 and all 368 payload bytes, excluding magic at 0x171 and the stored byte) & 0xFF. C accumulator is char (mod-256 addition, signedness irrelevant). File offset of stored byte is 0x175 (373) after per-block byte reversal; covered file bytes are the block-reversed equivalents. Decompiled proof: FUN_080237a0 loop 'cVar3 = param_1[uVar4] + cVar3' while index < 0x171, then 'if (param_1[0x172] == cVar3) struct+0x88 = 1'.

io_driver_functions.notes: Synchronous DMA3 engine (SAD/DAD/CNT via literal-pool pointers to 0x040000D4 region, enable bit 0x80000000, busy-poll) with WAITCNT (0x04000204) timing setup; used in both directions between RAM and EEPROM window 0x0D000000 by the read routine. Role 'write' denotes DMA transfer; it is the shared transfer primitive, CONFIRMED_STATIC on register identity.

SDK EEPROM_V124 read of one 8-byte block: block-index < block-count at config+4 (64), address-bit count at config+8 (6 for 4Kbit); DMA-out command/address bitstream (halfword LSBs, two leading 1 bits), DMA-in 0x44 halfwords from 0x0D000000, packs 64 bits MSB-first into 4 u16s stored at dest+6,+4,+2,+0 (per-block byte reversal vs file image). Returns 0 on success.

Reads all 64 blocks (buf + block*8), aborts on first non-zero return, calls FUN_080237a0 to deserialize/validate, then booleanizes struct+0x83 to 1 iff it (after substitution) equals 'W'. Bracketed by guard pair FUN_080485d0/FUN_08048634 (role hypothesized DMA/audio quiesce). Vestigial args 0xff and 1 are ignored by callees.

Clears struct+0x88 (valid), copies buf[0] to struct+0x83, memcpy(payload_dst, buf+1, 0x170) via FUN_08049a9c, sums buf[0..0x170], substitutes buf[0x171] into struct+0x83 if it was 'W', sets struct+0x88=1 iff buf[0x172]==sum8. Payload is copied even when the checksum fails.
Same function as above; hosts the only checksum computation in the corpus (sum8, see checksums array). Writer-side computation must be identical but lives in unrecovered 0x08023624.

Load-save entry: CpuSet (SWI 0x0B via 0x08049424) staging, clears struct+0x83/+0x84/+0x88, FUN_080235a4 EEPROM init (func_0x0804943c(4), hypothesized 4Kbit select), FUN_080235b4 read-all+validate, sets struct+0x84=1 on success. No caller recovered (jumptable/function-table dispatch; cf. FUN_08023a30 table dispatch).

Deferred-save state machine on struct+0x8c: state 1 arms 0x7a (122) countdown and CpuSet-stages the image; state 2 calls serializer func_0x08023624(struct+0x82 byte, ...) and returns to state 0. Trigger (who sets state 1) not in corpus.

Serializer + EEPROM-write flush. NOT among the 162 decompiled functions (referenced only as func_0x08023624); the SDK EEPROM-write routine is likewise absent. Its net effects are verified from the completed .sav image: stamp 'W' at logical 0 and 369, sum8 at logical 370, full 512-byte image written block-ascending (proven by mid-write snapshot sav-00).
Word-optimized memcpy; used for the 368-byte payload copy on load (and unrelated copies elsewhere).

struct+0x84 = load-completed flag (set on read success regardless of checksum)
struct+0x88 = valid flag (1 iff sum8 matches)
payload struct (memcpy dest _DAT_08023804, 368 bytes from logical image 0x001..0x170)

No callers in callgraph; identity with the memcpy payload destination cannot be proven because _DAT_ bases are unresolved. FUN_08000638 is a sibling default initializer with a compatible footprint.

fields.name: magic_primary
fields.update_mechanism: Stamped 'W' (0x57) by serializer 0x08023624 on save (code not recovered; effect verified). On load, copied to save-manager struct+0x83 by FUN_080237a0 and tested against 'W'.
fields.evidence: FUN_080237a0: '*(S+0x83) = *buf; if (*(S+0x83) == 'W') *(S+0x83) = buf[0x171]'; FUN_080235b4 booleanizes it. Logical offset 0 maps to file offset 0x007 under FUN_08049504's per-block byte reversal; both .sav files hold 0x57 there.

fields.name: payload_first_byte_suspected_version
fields.update_mechanism: Part of the 368-byte payload memcpy'd verbatim (FUN_080237a0). FUN_080234b0 writes u16 0x0032 at its struct start, which would produce exactly the observed payload bytes 0x32 0x00 if that struct is the payload struct.
fields.evidence: Observed 0x32 in both saves; FUN_080234b0 '*puVar1 = 0x32' (u16) in ghidra/decompiled.c. No code in the corpus reads or compares this byte, so a checked version tag is unproven; a stat value of 50 is equally consistent.

fields.name: payload_body_opaque

observed_values.saves/sav-00-f1613.sav: mostly 0x00; 0x01 at logical 0x005,0x00D,0x00E,0x061,0x062,0x0B5,0x0B6; 0xFF cluster near logical 0x003..0x008

fields.update_mechanism: Copied verbatim between EEPROM image (logical 0x001..0x170) and RAM payload struct by FUN_080237a0 memcpy (load) and serializer 0x08023624 (save). Interior mutations by gameplay code are outside the corpus.
fields.evidence: FUN_080237a0 'func_0x08049a9c(_DAT_08023804, param_1 + 1, 0x170)' in ghidra/decompiled.c; byte census computed from both .sav files after block-reversal transform. RAM destination literal unresolved, hence ram_addr null.

fields.name: payload_flag_a
fields.update_mechanism: Payload-struct offset 0x004; written as part of the verbatim payload image. No interpreter in corpus.
fields.evidence: One of only seven non-0x00/0xFF payload bytes in either save (Python byte census); boolean-like value 0x01.

fields.name: payload_flag_pair_b
fields.update_mechanism: Payload-struct offsets 0x00C..0x00D; verbatim payload. Hypothesized same flag in sub-record 0 of three (0x54 stride, cf. FUN_080234b0).
fields.evidence: Adjacent 0x01 pair; payload-relative offset 0x00C, and the three pairs at payload offsets 0x00C/0x060/0x0B4 are exactly 0x54 apart, matching FUN_080234b0's 3-entry x 0x54-byte stride.

fields.name: payload_flag_pair_c
fields.update_mechanism: Payload-struct offsets 0x060..0x061; verbatim payload. Hypothesized same flag in sub-record 1 of three (0x54 stride).
fields.evidence: Adjacent 0x01 pair exactly 0x54 after payload_flag_pair_b; see FUN_080234b0 stride analysis.

fields.name: payload_flag_pair_d
fields.update_mechanism: Payload-struct offsets 0x0B4..0x0B5; verbatim payload. Hypothesized same flag in sub-record 2 of three (0x54 stride).
fields.evidence: Adjacent 0x01 pair exactly 0x54 after payload_flag_pair_c; see FUN_080234b0 stride analysis.

fields.name: payload_erased_looking_region
fields.update_mechanism: Inside the checksummed payload (logical 0x150..0x16F); the RAM image itself holds 0xFF here in the completed, valid save. Never interpreted by corpus code (only summed).
fields.evidence: Both .sav files hold 0xFF across logical 0x150..0x16F even though sav-01 is fully written and checksum-valid; therefore payload data (reserved space or 0xFF/-1 sentinel fields), not unwritten media.

fields.name: magic_secondary

observed_values.saves/sav-00-f1613.sav: 0xFF (erased, file offset 0x176) - write not yet complete

fields.update_mechanism: Stamped 'W' by serializer near the end of the block-ascending flush (EEPROM block 46 of 64). On load, FUN_080237a0 substitutes it into struct+0x83 when magic_primary=='W', yielding a net double-'W' presence check booleanized by FUN_080235b4.
fields.evidence: FUN_080237a0 'if (*(char *)(_DAT_08023800 + 0x83) == 'W') *(char *)(_DAT_08023800 + 0x83) = param_1[0x171]'; sav-01 holds 0x57 at the transformed file offset, sav-00 still holds erased 0xFF.

fields.name: checksum_sum8

observed_values.saves/sav-00-f1613.sav: stored 0xFF (erased, file offset 0x175); computed 0x27; loader would reject

fields.update_mechanism: Computed by serializer over logical 0x000..0x170 on save (code not recovered); recomputed and compared by FUN_080237a0 on load, setting struct+0x88=1 on match.
fields.evidence: FUN_080237a0 sum loop + 'if (param_1[0x172] == cVar3)'; Python verification executed on both .sav files (see SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md section 4.3): sav-01 computed 0x60 == stored 0x60; naive file-order sum gives 0x61, independently confirming the block-reversal transform.

fields.name: image_tail_zero_filled
fields.update_mechanism: Remainder of the 512-byte EEPROM image beyond the single 371-byte record; written as zeros by a completed flush, never read/summed/validated by any corpus function.
fields.evidence: Byte census of both .sav files; FUN_080237a0 reads at most logical 0x172 and FUN_080235b4 validates nothing beyond it. The sav-00->sav-01 0xFF->0x00 transition over this range is the clearest block-ascending write-progress marker.

fields.name: ram_save_present_flag
fields.update_mechanism: RAM-only field at save-manager struct+0x83 (absolute address unknown; offset -1 denotes not an EEPROM offset). Cleared by FUN_08023824, set from image bytes by FUN_080237a0, booleanized to 0/1 by FUN_080235b4. 1 iff both magics are 'W', independent of checksum.
fields.evidence: Decompiled stores at _DAT_08023800+0x83 / _DAT_08023608+0x83 in FUN_08023824/FUN_080237a0/FUN_080235b4 (two literals for the same struct; bases unresolved).

fields.name: ram_load_completed_flag

observed_values.derived: 1 after any successful EEPROM read, even checksum-failing

fields.update_mechanism: RAM-only field at struct+0x84. Cleared at load entry, set to 1 when FUN_080235a4 and FUN_080235b4 both return 0. Does NOT imply checksum validity.

fields.name: ram_save_valid_flag
fields.update_mechanism: RAM-only field at struct+0x88. Cleared by FUN_08023824 and at FUN_080237a0 entry; set to 1 iff sum8 over logical 0x000..0x170 equals stored byte at 0x172. The loader's only integrity verdict.
fields.evidence: FUN_080237a0 '*(undefined4 *)(_DAT_08023800 + 0x88) = 0; ... if (param_1[0x172] == cVar3) *(undefined4 *)(iVar1 + 0x88) = 1'; verdict reproduced in Python for both saves.

fields.name: ram_save_state_and_serializer_arg

observed_values.derived: state byte struct+0x8c cycles 1->2->0 during deferred save; struct+0x82 byte passed to serializer

fields.update_mechanism: RAM-only fields at struct+0x8c (deferred-save state machine state) and struct+0x82 (sole argument byte to serializer 0x08023624, meaning unknown - possibly slot index or dirty flag, but no slot mechanism exists in the verified format).
fields.evidence: FUN_0802388c body in ghidra/decompiled.c: state 1 arms 0x7a countdown + CpuSet; state 2 'func_0x08023624(*(undefined1 *)(_DAT_080238bc + 0x82), uRam080238e8)'. Trigger and arg semantics unrecovered.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: File offset 0x007 (logical 0x000, magic_primary): 0x57 -> 0x00 in sav-01, once without and once with checksum repair (recompute sum8 over logical 0x000..0x170, store at file 0x175)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Save treated as absent (RAM struct+0x83=0) in both variants, proving magic_primary gates presence independently of the checksum verdict (struct+0x88).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: File offset 0x176 (logical 0x171=369, magic_secondary): 0x57 -> 0x00 in sav-01; no repair needed or possible (byte is outside the summed range)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Discriminator test: checksum stays valid (struct+0x88=1) but presence boolean struct+0x83 becomes 0. Reveals whether game consumers key on presence, validity, or both.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: File offset 0x175 (logical 0x172=370, stored checksum): 0x60 -> 0x61 in sav-01
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: struct+0x88=0 while struct+0x83 stays 1. If the game still loads the save, consumers ignore the checksum flag (robustness finding); if it rejects, the checksum is enforced.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: File offset 0x002 (logical 0x005, payload_flag_a): 0x01 -> 0x00 in sav-01, with checksum repair at file 0x175
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Save still validates; exactly one gameplay/UI trait should differ after load. Repeat for file 0x00A/0x009 (logical 0x00D/0x00E), 0x066/0x065 (logical 0x061/0x062), 0x0B2/0x0B1 (logical 0x0B5/0x0B6) to map all four observed 0x01 flags; probe value 0x02/0xFF afterwards to distinguish boolean vs enum/counter.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: File offset 0x006 (logical 0x001, suspected version byte): 0x32 -> 0x33 in sav-01, with checksum repair at file 0x175
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If the save still loads, 0x32 is unchecked payload data (e.g. a stat of 50); rejection despite valid magics+checksum would falsify the current reader model by revealing a version check outside FUN_080237a0.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Logical 0x150..0x16F (payload_erased_looking_region; file blocks at 0x150,0x158,0x160,0x168 with per-block byte reversal): 0xFF x32 -> 0x00 x32 in sav-01, with checksum repair at file 0x175
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: No observable change if the region is reserved payload; changed gameplay state if it holds 0xFF/-1 sentinel fields. Start with one 8-byte block (logical 0x150..0x157, file 0x157..0x150) to localize.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: File offset 0x1F8 (tail, logical 0x17F area): 0x00 -> 0x42 in sav-01; tail is outside the summed range
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Zero observable effect, confirming logical 0x173..0x1FF is dead image space. Any effect implies an undocumented second structure beyond the single record.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Counterfactual control: boot with saves/sav-00-f1613.sav (genuine mid-write image: magic_primary present, magic_secondary and checksum still erased 0xFF) unmodified, ideally reloading from states/sav-01-pre.ss (frame 1613)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Treated as no valid save (struct+0x83=0, struct+0x88=0), confirming torn-write rejection and the total absence of backup/salvage logic.

open_questions: Serializer/EEPROM-write path not in corpus: func_0x08023624 (invoked by FUN_0802388c state 2) and the SDK EEPROM_V124 write routine (expected near 0x08049504) were not trace-decompiled; writer internals, per-block write timing, and any write-verify step are unrecovered. Net writer effects are verified only from the .sav images.

Absolute RAM addresses are unknown for every struct: Ghidra left all _DAT_080xxxxx/puRam literals unresolved, so the save-manager struct (_DAT_08023800/_DAT_080238bc), payload destination (_DAT_08023804), and buffer addresses cannot be given as 0x02xxxxxx/0x03xxxxxx values, and it cannot be proven whether the payload destination equals the manager struct plus an offset.

Payload interior semantics (368 bytes) are unmapped: no corpus code interprets any payload byte. The three 0x01 flag pairs spaced exactly 0x54 apart (payload offsets 0x00C, 0x060, 0x0B4) and FUN_080234b0's 3x0x54-byte entry stride suggest three sub-records, but this is hypothesis only.

Whether FUN_08000638 and/or FUN_080234b0 initialize the actual save payload struct (vs an unrelated gameplay struct) cannot be proven from unresolved literals; FUN_080234b0 writing 0x0032 at its struct start matches payload bytes 0x32 0x00 but is not conclusive.

Save trigger unknown: who sets save-manager struct+0x8c=1, the meaning of the struct+0x82 byte passed to the serializer, the exact caller of load entry FUN_08023824, and the ignored 0xff / 1 arguments in the FUN_08023824 -> FUN_080235b4 -> FUN_080237a0 chain.

Role of the FUN_080485d0/FUN_08048634 guard pair bracketing EEPROM reads (hypothesis: DMA3/audio quiesce, +10/-10 counter and 0x400/0xb600 register pokes) and of func_0x0804943c(4) beyond EEPROM chip-type selection (argument 4 matches the 4Kbit part and the 512-byte images).

Whether gameplay consumers check the valid flag (struct+0x88), only the presence boolean (struct+0x83), or neither: the payload is memcpy'd into RAM before checksum validation, so a checksum-failing save's payload reaches RAM regardless. Fuzzing targets F2/F3 in SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md section 6 are designed to resolve this.

No second sample pair exists for a different gameplay state, so payload change-mapping (which bytes move with progress/time/party state) and any generation counter that only changes across distinct save events (rather than within one flush) cannot be ruled out from these two snapshots of a single write.
